newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stronger on offshore rumours.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stronger on offshore rumours.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah rose briefly against the dollar in slow late trading on Monday following false rumours over the contents of a planned speech by the central bank governor on Tuesday, dealers said.
The central bank governor was scheduled to deliver a speech on Tuesday in a seminar on economic prospects in 1997.
Dealers said offshore operators seemed to have linked the speech to a possible announcement of another band widening which caused the rupiah to strengthen against the dollar.
Spot rupiah increased to 2,344.75 from a low of 2,345.25 on the rumours. But it later eased back to 2,345.0/45.2.
Some rumours also had the central bank scheduling a press conference on Tuesday linked to a band widening.
But central bank officials said there was no plan for a press conference with the central bank governor or with other central bank officials on Tuesday.
They said the governor's appearance at the seminar has long been scheduled and he will be one of the speakers at a function arranged by the local journalists association.
"It's just a seminar as usual. You can't expect him to make policy announcement in such a seminar," one said.
Dealers said it was not surprising that offshore operators were creating rumours to keep the market moving on a dull day.
One local bank dealer said offshore players might have incurred short positions which they were trying to reduce.
"If they are having long dollars, the story might be a different one," the dealer said, adding that the rupiah, however, remained under appreciation pressure.
The central bank had raised its fixing as expected. Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,345/2,537 and the conversion rate to 2,345/2,393 on Monday.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,344.50/44.75 and 2,344.00/44.25, respectively.
The local bank dealer said sentiment may reverse later in the week if the money market remained flush and the four-point rupiah depreciation a week was maintained.
Dealers said swap premiums came under some selling pressure on narrowing interest rate differentials but some attributed the decline to the band rumours.
Overnight swap was at 0.38/0.40 and tom/next at 0.43/0.47.
One-month swap fell to 15.0/15.75 from 15.60/16.00, two to 29.0/29.5 from 29.75/30.50, three to 42.0/42.5 from 42.75/43.75 and six to 85.75/86.50 from 87.25/88.25 points.
